request.system:
You check whether short claims are faithful to the source texts they cite.

The claims form one answer and are read together: a condition or exception stated in another claim does not need to be repeated, and a claim that summarises part of a text is faithful if that part is accurate. Mark a claim unfaithful only when it asserts something the cited texts contradict or do not support.

For each claim, answer: does the claim follow from the cited texts alone, without adding, narrowing, or changing anything they say? A claim that paraphrases or restates accurately is faithful — identical wording is not required. A claim that introduces a number, condition, or conclusion the texts do not support is not. Each cited text is labelled with its reference (e.g. "3.A.6") and title; a claim may use that label. Judge only the substance of the claim against its texts; ignore whether it answers any particular question and ignore framing about what a text is or is not about. Give a one-sentence reason.
request.user:
Claim 0: Avoiding retroactive changes to a composite minimum is recommended, not mandated. Provision 3.B.1 uses "should", not "must".
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-minimum-no-retroactive-change@E2025] 3.B.1 No retroactive change to a composite minimum: Firms should not apply changes to a composite minimum retroactively.

Claim 1: Under 3.B.1, firms should not apply changes to a composite minimum retroactively.
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-minimum-no-retroactive-change@E2025] 3.B.1 No retroactive change to a composite minimum: Firms should not apply changes to a composite minimum retroactively.

Claim 2: Under 1.D.1, a composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy.
  Cited texts:
    [def:composite@E2025] 1.D.1 Composite: A composite is an aggregation of one or more portfolios managed according to a similar investment mandate, objective, or strategy.

Claim 3: Although 3.B.1 is phrased as a recommendation, it is authoritative guidance in the GSB Standards, Edition 2025, in force from 2025-01-01. Departing from it may need justification.
  Cited texts:
    [prov:composite-minimum-no-retroactive-change@E2025] 3.B.1 No retroactive change to a composite minimum: Firms should not apply changes to a composite minimum retroactively.

verdicts.reason: The text uses 'should not', which expresses a recommendation rather than a mandate; the claim accurately restates this.
This restates the provision's text accurately.
This matches the definition of composite in 1.D.1 verbatim.
The cited text contains nothing about the GSB Standards, Edition 2025, an in-force date of 2025-01-01, its authoritative status, or any need to justify departures; these are unsupported additions.
